perspective:
From Brandon Talayumptewa’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is an insurance agent. He met Benjamin Erickson professionally when Benjamin sought business insurance advice.
- In their first meeting, Benjamin wanted comprehensive business coverage and said some terms were new. Brandon explained liability insurance as a safety net, gave a slip-and-fall example, and explained asset protection as guarding inventory and equipment. Benjamin said this made sense, asked for an example, said it simplified things, and thanked him. Brandon was concerned about communicating complex details effectively because he was aware Benjamin had limited formal education.
- In a later meeting, Brandon had revised his view of Benjamin’s ability to understand detailed information and felt more confident. He explained business interruption insurance as covering income loss when operations are interrupted, and property insurance as covering damages and theft. Benjamin said he had been reading up, called business interruption crucial in unpredictable times, and found the comprehensive coverage reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, Brandon felt insecure about how Benjamin perceived his cautious, detail-oriented nature and tried to keep things engaging. Benjamin said he appreciated Brandon’s thoroughness and also enjoyed lighter moments. Brandon told a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for a million dollars. Benjamin reacted with interest and said it made sense considering the stakes. Brandon said it was about assessing risks, even unusual ones, though less unusual than Benjamin’s business; Benjamin agreed.
- Feeling pleased by Benjamin’s positive response to his personal anecdote, Brandon decided to offer support beyond insurance. He suggested strategic investments that could lower premiums, such as upgrading security systems to protect assets and reduce insurance costs. Benjamin said he was all ears, called Brandon’s insights invaluable, said he had not considered that but it sounded smart, called it a win-win, and agreed to explore it.
- Encouraged by their strong rapport and mutual benefits, Brandon felt optimistic and proposed a joint venture: co-developing a platform that integrates risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed, called the idea groundbreaking, said combining their expertise could set them apart, and agreed to draft initial plans.

Brandon does not have access to Benjamin’s private thoughts, exact internal reasoning, or any information not stated or shown in their interactions.
